sections.h2: The county and its housing market
sections.html:
Sweetwater County covers southwestern Wyoming along the Colorado and Utah lines and is the state's largest county by area, with about 4 people per square mile. An estimated 41,267 residents lived there in mid-2025. Green River is the county seat, with 11,825 people in 2020, and Rock Springs is the biggest city at 23,526.

About 74.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied home value is $251,400, and there are 17,502 households. A parcel might be a city lot in Rock Springs or land far from any town, yet both are handled by the same two courthouse offices in Green River.

Trona mining and soda ash production anchor the local economy, so much of the tax base sits in plants and mines rather than houses.

sections.h2: How your house is assessed and taxed
sections.html:
The Sweetwater County Assessor values every taxable parcel as of January 1, and a house is taxed on 9.5 percent of that value. The Assessor follows Wyoming statutes and Department of Revenue guidelines, while voters, commissioners and state limits set the tax rates. Your bill is the assessed value multiplied by the mills, and residential mill levies commonly fall between 65 and 80.

  • Homes and other real and personal property: 9.5 percent of market value.
  • Industrial property, including mineral processing: 11.5 percent.
  • Minerals and mine products: 100 percent.

The Assessor values property but does not bill or collect. The Treasurer does.

Homeowners can stack several reductions, and they appear at the bottom of the notice of value. The 25 percent reduction from Senate File 69 was applied automatically in 2025, and a later round required an affidavit filed with the county assessor by March 1. Call the Assessor at 307-872-3700 to learn the current process.

  • The veteran's exemption rose from $3,000 to $6,000 for tax year 2025. Anyone who does not see it on the notice should contact the Assessor.
  • The long-term homeowners exemption is for owners age 65 who have paid Wyoming property taxes for 25 years and live in the home eight months a year. Bring ID that shows a birthdate.
  • The Property Tax Refund Program pays up to half the median residential tax or 75 percent of the bill, whichever is less. Taxes must be paid in full before applying.

You have 30 days from the date the notice of value was mailed to contact the Assessor and make your case. Wyoming Statute 39-13-109 calls for a written statement of why the assessment is incorrect. Notices usually go out in the spring.

A short checklist helps:

  • Find your parcel's value and exemptions on the notice.
  • Collect recent sales of comparable Rock Springs or Green River homes.
  • Document condition problems with photos and bids.
  • Send your written statement before the 30 days end.

Statements are mailed in September. You can pay in full by December 31 or in two halves. Weekend and holiday due dates move to the next business day, and mailed payments must be postmarked by the due date.

Payment optionDue date
Full year, one paymentDecember 31
First halfNovember 10
Second halfMay 10

May 11 is the delinquency date for the second half. View or pay a statement online at itax.sweetwatercountywy.gov. Real property taxes are a lien on the house, so any unpaid balance gets settled when the property sells.

The notice arrives in the spring and shows your parcel's value for the year, with every exemption listed at the bottom. Check it the day it comes. If an exemption you qualify for is missing, call the Assessor right away rather than waiting for the tax bill, because the appeal window is only 30 days from the mailing date.

If you disagree with the value itself, the comparable-sales approach works best. Recent sales of similar Rock Springs or Green River houses, plus photos and bids for any condition problems, give the Assessor something concrete to review. A written statement of why the figure is wrong should accompany them.

sections.h2: Cold-weather care for a vacant house
sections.html: The area is semi-arid and cold, with Rock Springs averaging 10.45 inches of precipitation and 31.3 inches of snow a year. Freezing cold at roughly 6,000 feet is hard on roofs, pipes and furnaces, and an empty house can develop trouble fast. If you are carrying an inherited or vacant property, keep the heat on and have the roof checked while the tax bill sits unpaid.

sections.h2: Step by step: selling with a tax balance
sections.html:
Here is how the process usually runs when taxes are still owed on the house.

  1. Ask the Treasurer for the payoff figure, and confirm whether one half or both halves are open.
  2. Gather your mortgage payoff statement and any lien paperwork.
  3. Choose a buyer and a closing date, then give the title company the payoff figures.
  4. At closing, the title company pays the tax balance and any loan from your proceeds.
  5. You receive what is left after those payoffs.

Heirs sometimes find the tax bill unpaid because the owner died or moved away. The same steps apply, with one addition: the person signing the deed needs the paperwork that shows authority to sell.

sections.h2: Selling a Sweetwater County house with taxes due
sections.html:
Start by getting a payoff figure from the Treasurer, then decide how to close. An unpaid balance can be paid from the sale proceeds at the title company, and a cash buyer can purchase the house as-is without repairs. A cash sale skips the showings and the repair list, and the tax payoff is simply one more line on the closing statement.

Before you call, have your parcel number or address handy, plus any mortgage payoff statement. Offices to contact, all in the Green River courthouse at 80 W. Flaming Gorge Way:

  • Treasurer, Suite 139: 307-872-3720, taxes@sweetwatercountywy.gov
  • Assessor, Suite 122: 307-872-3700, assessor@sweetwatercountywy.gov
  • Rock Springs Assessor line: 307-922-5200

Call us at (424) 435-2326 if you want a written cash offer for a Sweetwater County house.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Sweetwater County, Wyoming?
faqs.a: The County Treasurer in Green River. The Assessor values property but does not set tax amounts or collect them.

faqs.q: How long do I have to question my Sweetwater County notice of value?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the date the notice was mailed. Wyoming Statute 39-13-109 calls for a written statement, so contact the Assessor at 307-872-3700 well before the window closes.

faqs.q: What is the residential assessment rate in Sweetwater County?
faqs.a: 9.5 percent of market value. Industrial property is assessed at 11.5 percent and mineral production at 100 percent.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Sweetwater County house if I owe property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance has to be paid or settled at closing, and the Treasurer can give you a payoff amount.

faqs.q: Is there a veteran's exemption in Sweetwater County?
faqs.a: Yes. It rose from $3,000 to $6,000 for tax year 2025. If you do not see it on your notice, contact the Assessor's office.
